sources.title: Introducing GPT-5 for developers
sources.evidence: Dated August 7, 2025. Explicitly makes the non-reasoning ChatGPT model available as gpt-5-chat-latest, distinct from the GPT-5 reasoning API model and the complete ChatGPT router system. Establishes original API release and non-reasoning identity. Reopened October 27, 2026; the release supplies no nominal total or active count and explicitly distinguishes this alias from the reasoning API model, including its minimal-reasoning setting.

sources.title: GPT-5 Chat model documentation
sources.evidence: Full HTML and Markdown read. Exact alias is marked shut down and points to the GPT-5 snapshot previously used in ChatGPT. Both formats label context 128,000, output limit 16,384, text/image input, text output and function calling supported. Markdown additionally lists maximum input 272,000, conflicting with its context label; this is preserved as a documentation inconsistency. Rechecked October 27, 2026 through the exact official documentation and fresh full Markdown cache; neither gives total or active parameter counts or a counted base-model lineage.

sources.title: API deprecations: July 2026 shutdown
sources.evidence: April 22, 2026 notice explicitly lists gpt-5-chat-latest for July 23, 2026 API shutdown. This is documentary service history, not a live endpoint test.

sources.title: GPT-5 System Card, August 13, 2025 revision
sources.evidence: Full PDF downloaded and text-extracted. Introduction distinguishes fast gpt-5-main from gpt-5-thinking and the router; model-data/training and comparison sections disclose no production parameter counts or architectural structure for the fast model. A whole-document parameter/architecture/Transformer search found no such disclosure. Rechecked the fresh October 27 PDF text, introduction, model-data/training section and comparison tables. The router chooses between distinct models; it is not evidence of within-model expert activation or an MoE parameter count.

sources.title: GPT-5.1 Instant and GPT-5.1 Thinking System Card Addendum
sources.evidence: Full November 12, 2025 PDF downloaded and text-extracted. Later comparison tables identify GPT-5 Instant August/October revisions but provide evaluation scores, not production counts or architecture. The new adaptive reasoning of GPT-5.1 Instant is not transferred to this earlier GPT-5 Chat alias. Rechecked the fresh October 27 complete extracted text and exact predecessor comparison tables; neither a total nor an activated-parameter column is present.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Current sections 2.2 and 9.1 grant limited hosted API usage and reserve service IP rights. Supports a descriptive proprietary classification rather than a checkpoint license; does not imply these exact current terms governed the August 2025 launch.

sources.title: Foundry Models sold by Azure: GPT-5 Chat historical specifications
sources.evidence: Provider table separately identifies GPT-5 Chat August 7 and October 3, 2025 versions, each with 128,000 context, 16,384 output and text/image-to-text interface. Corroborates the OpenAI context label; Azure retirement dates and version IDs are not substituted for the OpenAI alias history.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Complete Markdown read. Responses and Chat Completions accept PDF files for vision-capable models; the API extracts text and page images. Combined with exact GPT-5 Chat vision and endpoint support, this establishes PDF as an API file format, not a native sensory modality.

sources.title: AgenticEval: Toward Agentic and Self-Evolving Safety Evaluation of Large Language Models
sources.publisher: Yixu Wang et al.; Findings of ACL 2026
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Original research Table 3, PDF page 12, separately lists GPT-5 and exact GPT-5-chat-latest; the Parameters (B) entry for GPT-5-chat-latest is N/D. No active-count column is supplied. This later research comparison corroborates the unresolved size, not an OpenAI parameter disclosure.

sources.title: A Self-Controlled Benchmark of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models on Clinical Guideline Questions
sources.publisher: Andreas Vollmer et al.; Diagnostics, August 4, 2026
sources.evidence: Read October 27, 2026. Section 2.4 identifies the transparent-pipeline model as gpt-5-chat-latest. Table 2 gives GPT-5-chat Parameters N/A, explicitly defined as not publicly disclosed. Its note says this column measures total size and active counts can differ; it supplies no numeric active count for GPT-5 Chat. Used as a later original benchmark check, not developer disclosure or a basis to merge its RAG systems with this alias.

sources.title: LLMRouterBench: A Massive Benchmark and Unified Framework for LLM Routing
sources.publisher: Hao Li et al.; Findings of ACL 2026
sources.evidence: Read October 27, 2026. Original research Table 11, PDF page 17, distinguishes GPT-5-chat from GPT-5-medium and gives API input/output prices, not parameter counts. Table 10 reports sizes for a separate open-model pool; those counts cannot transfer to GPT-5 Chat. No total or active count for this chat model is established by the inspected comparison tables.

name.note: Catalog display name identifies the exact gpt-5-chat-latest alias. Latest is part of its identifier, not a claim that it is currently the latest ChatGPT model.

developer.note: Released and documented by OpenAI; Azure is a provider, not the developer.

family.note: The original release places this non-reasoning chat model within GPT-5, while distinguishing it from the thinking model and router system.

release_date.note: The dated original developer announcement explicitly makes the exact alias available. Later ChatGPT snapshot updates and retirement dates do not replace first API availability.

open_weights.note: The documented release is a closed hosted API model under service access terms; it does not distribute an open checkpoint.

license.note: Descriptive hosted-model classification, not an SPDX identifier or a downloadable-weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 recheck of the exact API documentation, original launch/system card, later GPT-5.1 comparisons and bounded original-research searches found no supported nominal total or counted-base lineage for this non-reasoning chat alias. AgenticEval explicitly marks its size N/D; the August 2026 clinical benchmark marks the exact alias N/A (not publicly disclosed). No reasoning-model value, later Instant sibling, rumor, energy scenario or capacity estimate is substituted.

active_parameters_b.note: Active count was searched separately on October 27 using gpt-5-chat-latest, GPT-5 Chat, gpt-5-main and GPT-5 Instant identities, including activated/active-parameter terms and later original comparison tables. None supplied a supported numeric active count for this exact model. The ChatGPT router selects separate models; it does not establish an MoE architecture or per-token count. Total-to-active equality and sibling transfers are not inferred.

architecture.note: Exact alias, gpt-5-main and GPT-5 Instant searches across first-party training and interpretability material did not establish a technical architecture for this model. Original and later cards disclose no structure; generic GPT-5 reasoning or Transformer explanations do not identify this separate fast chat model.

context_window.note: Correct the baseline 400,000 to the explicit 128,000 context label in both exact OpenAI HTML and Markdown, corroborated by both Azure historical Chat versions. OpenAI Markdown separately lists 272,000 maximum input, an internal conflict retained in notes; do not add it to the output cap or use it to infer a larger context.

modalities.note: Native text/image-to-text interface is exact-model documentation. PDF denotes supported API document input inferred from the official vision-model file rule plus exact vision/Responses support; the file is converted to text and page images. No native PDF, audio, video or generated-image output is inferred.

reasoning.note: The original announcement explicitly names gpt-5-chat-latest as the non-reasoning model. This corrects baseline true and concerns dedicated internal reasoning behavior, not ability to solve reasoning tasks. It is separate from GPT-5 minimal reasoning and later GPT-5.1 Instant adaptive reasoning.

tool_call.note: The current exact model page explicitly marks function calling supported in HTML and Markdown, correcting baseline false. This is last-documented historical capability; it does not establish identical support at first launch or current endpoint operation.

description.value: Non-reasoning GPT-5 Chat API model with text and image input, text output and function calling.
description.note: Identify the distinct chat model and its documented interface without transferring thinking-model features or making promotional claims.

patch.notes: The alias first became available August 7, 2025 as the non-reasoning GPT-5 model used in ChatGPT, separate from GPT-5 thinking and the full router system. Its documentation does not bind the last alias target to an immutable date. OpenAI labels its context 128,000 tokens and output cap 16,384; the Markdown also lists 272,000 maximum input, an unresolved internal inconsistency. The 128,000 context label is corroborated by Microsoft historical GPT-5 Chat specifications. Function calling is supported in the last-documented exact model page. PDF denotes API input processed as text and page images. OpenAI lists API shutdown on July 23, 2026; no live endpoint request was made. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed for this distinct chat model in OpenAI documentation and the inspected later research comparisons; the ChatGPT model-selection router does not establish an MoE count. Exact architecture remains unverified.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains explicit null total and active counts after fresh exact-model OpenAI evidence and later original research comparisons; no supported nominal count or counted-base lineage was found. Preserve the prior corrections to context (128,000), reasoning (false), function calling (true), family, license, PDF input and description, plus retirement and the conflicting Markdown maximum-input number. Exact chat-model architecture remains unverified.
